clue.text: A pound held back by debauchees for spending in the Soviet Union

definitions.text: for spending in the Soviet Union

indicators.note: the word for debauchees grips the pound abbreviation in its middle

parts.note: roués are dissolute rakes, debauchees

indicators.note: the pound abbreviation is turned round before going in

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Libertines in Soviet Russia squander their money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back' reads as one phrase meaning restrained, but 'held' is the container and 'back' turns the pound abbreviation; 'A pound' is a weight, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble was the currency of the USSR, the money people spent there.

clue.text: An engineer who plays a role at Dounreay, for instance

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
an actor performs a part

explanation.surface: An engineer moonlights as a performer at a nuclear site.
explanation.walkthrough: Dounreay is a nuclear power site on the north coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Dounreay housed nuclear fission units, so it exemplifies an atomic power plant.

clue.text: Somewhat lacking in humanity?

parts.note: seems to mean rather heartless, but means short of human beings, with too few inhabitants

explanation.surface: A person who is a bit inhumane.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparsely settled region has fewer residents than it could support.

clue.text: Nothing much about to plunder, apparently

indicators.note: around, so the word for much goes round the zero

parts.note: a lot is a great deal
O, the zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to rob, though there is little to take.
explanation.definitionFit: Booty is the goods taken by pillaging, and as a verb it means to pillage.

clue.text: Hunting for Arctic fauna, not freshwater fish?

parts.note: salt water rather than fresh is the sea
ling is a long marine fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Polar hunting that targets animals other than river fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting seals on the ice of polar waters is the activity of a sealer.

clue.text: Devoid of all warmth or affection

explanation.surface: Someone utterly without tenderness or love.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilly means lacking warmth; a head cold is an affection in the old medical sense of an ailment.

clue.text: Covering put round a metal tooth?

indicators.note: the word for a tooth is placed around the other two pieces

parts.note: a cog is a tooth on a gear wheel
tin is a metallic element

explanation.surface: A dentist's cap fitted over a metal tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of paint or film spread over a surface covers it.

clue.text: A bloomer that is purely symbolic

definitions.text: A bloomer that is purely symbolic

parts.words: A bloomer that is purely symbolic
parts.note: a flowering plant that serves as the emblem of purity; 'purely' points at what it stands for

explanation.surface: A mistake that is only a token gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: The white Madonna flower is a traditional emblem of chastity and innocence.

clue.text: Mercenary of coarse fibre

explanation.surface: A hired soldier wearing rough sacking.
explanation.definitionFit: German soldiers from Hesse hired by Britain were Hessians; hessian is a coarse jute cloth called burlap in America.

clue.text: Information that shouldn't be given to the public

definitions.text: Information that shouldn't be given to the public

parts.words: Information that shouldn't be given to the public
parts.note: a piece of classified government knowledge, protected by law from disclosure

explanation.surface: Data that must not be released to ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified state material covered by the Official Secrets Act must not be disclosed.

clue.text: Not one of us objects to add this to the statement

definitions.text: Not one of us objects to add this to the statement

parts.words: Not one of us objects to add this to the statement
parts.note: the phrase a group chimes in with to endorse a toast or a declaration unanimously

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees to tack a phrase onto a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The chorus is sung after 'For he's a jolly good fellow', voicing unanimous agreement with what was said.

clue.text: Place in Lebanon that may have to be blown up

definitions.text: that may have to be blown up

explanation.surface: A Lebanese town under threat of bombing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyre is an ancient Phoenician port in Lebanon; a wheel's pneumatic rubber ring is inflated with a pump.

clue.text: A creature that can fly, but not pass an exam?

explanation.surface: A flying animal that fails its test.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipit is a small songbird; to be 'pipped' in British slang is to be failed or beaten, so 'pip it' is to fail it.

clue.text: It repeatedly backs a South African primate

indicators.note: the reversed pair of letters is written down twice in a row
the word It is set going the other way

parts.note: taken as written, then turned

explanation.surface: Something keeps supporting an African monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' looks like 'supports' but turns IT into TI; 'repeatedly' doubles it. The titi is actually a South American monkey, so 'African' is the setter's slip.
explanation.definitionFit: The titi is a small long-tailed monkey, a primate of the forests of South America.

clue.text: West Indian dance in which people are forgotten

explanation.surface: A Caribbean dance where the dancers fade from memory.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trinidadian dance under a lowered bar shares its name with a state of neglect or oblivion.

clue.text: Unlooked for catches?

parts.note: reads like unexpected hauls, but means unforeseen drawbacks or the hooks on which clothing tears

explanation.surface: Fish caught without anyone searching.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden problems are unexpected obstacles, and a jagged point catches cloth.

clue.text: Go in for modified coverage

indicators.note: changed in form, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone chooses an altered insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiles or slates over a building are its overhead covering, the material on top.

clue.text: Peculiar tinge associated with an Alpine flower

indicators.note: strange or odd, so the letters of tinge come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd shade of colour seen on a mountain bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentians are blue-flowered plants of high mountain meadows, famously in the Alps.

clue.text: Type of chocolate biscuit still produced in Kentucky

explanation.surface: A chocolate cookie made somewhere in Kentucky.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bourbon is a British chocolate-cream sandwich biscuit; bourbon whiskey is distilled in Kentucky, a still being distilling apparatus.

clue.text: Scottish peak in which there's not enough char, possibly

indicators.note: the mountain word contains the other piece

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain
lack is a shortage

explanation.surface: On a Scottish mountain there is a shortage of vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Charring something by fire darkens it, one way of making it dark.

clue.text: Uneconomic charge for a letter?

parts.note: a 'letter' is one who lets property, and a token fee is far below the market price

explanation.surface: Postage that costs too little to make sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A token sum paid to a landlord, much below market value, is a peppercorn payment.

clue.text: Flower girl after knocking some hard liquor back

indicators.note: the girl's name follows the reversed drink
knocking back a drink means downing it, and here the spirit's name is turned round
with knocking, signals the drink's name read backwards

parts.note: gin is a strong spirit
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl downing some gin after a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' reads as downing a drink, and it does double service in the surface; here it turns the spirit round before the girl's name follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigella, love-in-a-mist, is a garden plant with blue blooms.

clue.text: Gloomy god surrounded by crazy nature-lovers!

indicators.note: the god's name is placed inside the word for crazy

parts.note: nuts means mad
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld

explanation.surface: A dark deity among mad lovers of the outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists who go unclothed are nicknamed lovers of nature.

clue.text: One chorister was a wise old Trojan

parts.note: an means one
a tenor is a choir singer

explanation.surface: A choirboy who was a sage of ancient Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, Antenor is a sagacious elder counsellor of Troy.

clue.text: A stage-joke Samuel cut to pieces

parts.note: a gag is a comedian's joke

explanation.surface: A theatrical joke about a prophet carving someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1 Samuel 15 the prophet Samuel hews Agag, king of the Amalekites, in pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible names the Amalekite king whom the prophet hacked apart as Agag.

clue.text: A chemical I made in error

indicators.note: mistakenly, so the letters of the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to producing the wrong compound.
explanation.definitionFit: An amide is an organic compound derived from ammonia, a chemical substance.

clue.text: See 18
Intoxicating drink from the East Indies

indicators.note: the drink is taken out of a run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Liquor imported from the Indian Ocean islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine, an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: 21 turning fatuous in his dotage?

indicators.note: the answer to clue 21 is read backwards

parts.note: refers to the biblical king's name at 21 across

explanation.surface: An old man becoming foolish in his senility.
explanation.definitionFit: Senile and silly people are called doolally or dotty, which is this informal word.

clue.text: Remains calm and doesn't take a short cut?

explanation.surface: Someone stays cool and declines a quick route.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means stays unflustered; read literally it means not having one's hair trimmed.

clue.text: Clayey soil that is hard to cultivate

explanation.surface: Heavy clay ground that resists farming.
explanation.definitionFit: Boulder clay left by glaciers is called till; to till land is to plough and farm it.

clue.text: Wreck that's reassembled with little hesitation

indicators.note: put back together differently, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: er is the short sound of hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: A wrecked object put back together with some pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: To smash something into fragments is to destroy or ruin it.
